description: The English Housing Survey is a continuous national survey of people's housing circumstances and the condition and energy efficiency of housing in England, combining a household interview with a physical inspection of a sub-sample of properties. It is commissioned by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, with fieldwork by NatCen Social Research; it follows the Survey of English Housing, run annually from 1993, and marks 50 years since the first national housing survey of 1967. Each year a random sample of private addresses from Royal Mail lists is invited; headline and detailed reports and live tables of time series on tenure, condition and energy efficiency are published annually, with collection groups from 2008-09 to 2024-25. Coverage: England. Access: GOV.UK reports and live tables; microdata through the UK Data Service for secondary analysis by registered users. Licence: microdata under the UK Data Service End User Licence; published outputs free. Caveats: sample-based, so small-area estimates are not available from the survey itself. Simulation uses: stock condition and energy efficiency inputs for housing retrofit and resilience models. Related records: the Energy Follow Up Survey 2011 and the Scottish House Condition Survey.
